title: This Hidden Human ‘Sense’ Is Quietly Shaping Your Reality, Scientists Say
titleZh: 闭上眼，你能在脑中看见一个苹果吗
summary:
互联网上，苹果似乎已经成为测试想象力的参照物——更确切地说，是一种衡量心理意象的符号。经常有人在X或Reddit上发帖询问网友：如果让你想象一个苹果，你的脑海里会出现什么画面？人们的回复千差万别，有人能详细描绘出苹果的颜色与光泽，而另一些人则完全无法产生任何视觉画面。

来源：大众机械（节选）；作者：Elana Spivack；原文发布时间：2025-08-22 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Apples seem to have become the internet’s symbol for imagination—or at least, mental imagery. Every so often, someone takes to X or Reddit and asks what other users see when they imagine an apple. Responses may range from vivid descriptions of the apple’s coloration and shine to a complete absence of visual detail.
paragraphs.contentZh: 互联网上，苹果似乎已经成为测试想象力的参照物——更确切地说，是一种衡量心理意象的符号。经常有人在X或Reddit上发帖询问网友：如果让你想象一个苹果，你的脑海里会出现什么画面？人们的回复千差万别，有人能详细描绘出苹果的颜色与光泽，而另一些人则完全无法产生任何视觉画面。

paragraphs.contentEn: But what nobody seems to appreciate is the assumption that all responders are picturing an apple in their “mind’s eye.” In fact, about 1 to 3 percent of people experience an extreme form of “imagery vividness.” It could mean conjuring an image so vivid that it seems to have projected an apple into real life—or, on the opposite end of the spectrum, thinking about an apple in totally non-visual terms. Scientists are still seeking to understand the neurological mechanisms behind this wild variation, and how people navigate the world effectively no matter where on the scale their visualization lies.
paragraphs.contentZh: 但很少有人注意到其中隐含的前提，即默认所有回答者都能在“脑海中”看到一个苹果。实际上，大约1%至3%的人在“心理意象清晰度”上处于极端水平。也就是说，对于心理意象清晰度极高的人而言，想象可能鲜活到仿佛一个苹果真的浮现在眼前——相反，心理意象清晰度极低的人在想象苹果时完全不会有视觉画面。科学家仍在探索这种巨大差异背后的神经机制，以及无论人们的视觉化能力处于何种水平，为什么依然能有效理解并适应这个世界。

paragraphs.contentEn: When it comes to the neuroscience of imagination, “there’s a few different hypotheses floating around,” Wilma Bainbridge, Ph.D., a professor of psychology at the University of Chicago says, “but the commonly accepted idea is that seeing something in your mind’s eye is like the visual system working in reverse.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 芝加哥大学心理学教授威尔玛·班布里奇博士指出，关于想象力背后的神经科学，“目前存在几种不同的假说，但更普遍被接受的观点是，当你在脑海中想象某个事物时，本质上类似于视觉系统在反向运作。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The visual system begins with light entering the eye. Millions of nerve fibers that comprise the optic nerve process this information and relay it directly to the brain. The visual cortex resides in the occipital lobe, which is at the very back of the brain. When we see something, our brain starts with the object’s basic, concrete aspects, Bainbridge says. It begins with detecting lines and colors before categorizing the object verbally and understanding its relationship to other nearby objects. In that sense, the brain climbs the ladder of abstraction, assembling more basic concepts before reaching more complex levels that involve meaning.
paragraphs.contentZh: 视觉系统的运作始于光线进入眼睛。由数百万根神经纤维组成的视神经负责对光信号进行处理，并将信息直接传递至大脑。视觉皮层位于大脑后方的枕叶区域。班布里奇解释说，当我们看到一个物体时，大脑首先会处理其最基本、最具体的特征。从线条和颜色开始，再逐步用语言对其分类，并理解它与周围物体的关系。从这个意义上说，大脑的处理过程就像在攀登抽象的阶梯，先拼合最基础的概念，然后再走向更高层次，赋予物体意义。

paragraphs.contentEn: But when you switch from looking at an apple to visualizing one in your mind’s eye, this hypothesis says your brain might start with abstract concepts, first calling to mind what it wants to visualize, before moving to concrete characteristics like shape and color. A 2019 paper published in the journal Nature Reviews Neuroscience describes this process as “reverse visual hierarchy.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 然而，当你从在现实中观察苹果转为在脑海中想象它时，上述假说则认为，大脑可能会先从抽象概念入手，即先唤起想要看见什么，然后再逐步补充形状、颜色等具体特征。2019年发表在《自然·神经科学综述》上的一篇论文将这一过程称为“逆向视觉层级”。

paragraphs.contentEn: The apple test also introduces a spectrum of visual imagery, which shows two conditions that fall at either end: aphantasia and hyperphantasia. Those with aphantasia don’t see anything in their mind’s eye, while those with hyperphantasia imagine elaborately detailed objects and scenarios that seem almost lifelike. Yet, perception far extends beyond sight, pulling together other types of sensory information, like hearing and smell. So does our imagination, though research tends to favor visual imagery, according to the 2019 paper. Understanding the differences in brains of those with atypical imaginative capabilities, like aphantasia and hyperphantasia, can help provide greater insight into how humans create mental pictures.
paragraphs.contentZh: 苹果测试也揭示了视觉想象能力的连续区间，其两端分别对应两种极端情况：心盲症和超幻症。心盲症患者完全无法在脑海中形成视觉画面，而超幻症患者则能想象出极其精细的物体和场景，几乎与现实无异。不过，人类的感知并不仅限于视觉，还会整合听觉、嗅觉等多种感官信息。想象力同样如此，但2019年的那篇论文指出，相关研究往往更侧重于视觉层面。研究心盲症和超幻症等非典型想象能力的大脑差异，有助于我们更好地理解人类是如何在脑海中生成画面的。

paragraphs.contentEn: Researchers think they know at least one good reason for our powers of imagination, no matter how they manifest for each of us. Our ability to imagine things could be an extension of the ability to predict what we’re going to perceive. Prediction is important to anticipating what stimuli we might experience so we’ll know how to respond, says Shimon Edelman, Ph.D., a professor of psychology at Cornell University. Other animals need the ability to predict too, in order to know what’s out of the ordinary and worth paying attention to. But perhaps they don’t have the ability to imagine, at least the way we do, Edelman says.
paragraphs.contentZh: 无论想象能力在不同人身上如何表现，研究人员认为，他们至少找到了一个解释其存在的重要原因。我们的想象力，可能是预测能力的延伸，即预先模拟我们即将感知到的事物。康奈尔大学心理学教授西蒙·埃德尔曼博士指出，预测能力之所以关键，是因为它能帮助我们预判可能遇到的刺激，从而决定如何应对。其他动物同样需要预测能力，以便识别哪些情况异常并作出警觉。但埃德尔曼补充说，动物或许并不具备想象的能力，至少，不具备我们人类这样的想象能力。

paragraphs.contentEn: Yet, all the monsters, places, people, and scenarios we might imagine to be novel are actually simply composites of the vast amount of experiences we’ve processed during our lives, Bainbridge says. “If I have you visualize a purple elephant and a cup of milk, that all relates to something you’ve seen before, but you’re just combining them in unique ways.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 不过，班布里奇指出，我们想象出的那些看似新奇的怪物、场景、人物和情节，实际上都只是对过往经验的重新组合。她解释说：“如果我让你想象一头紫色的大象和一杯牛奶，这些元素都源自你曾经见过的事物，只是被你以一种独特的方式拼合在一起而已。”
